name: cpln
conclusion_quantitative: cpln (Escalate) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 3 autonomy limits, 2 clarification rules, 4 approval gates, 2 escalation rules; none for validation rules. Strongest: approval gates.
conclusion_qualitative: cpln deploys and manages containerized workloads across clouds with Control Plane: workloads, secrets, identities, firewalls, autoscaling and domains. Its rules guard against costly mistakes: confirm the target before mutating, get explicit confirmation of destructive operations, surface constraint conflicts rather than silently downgrading, and diagnose failures rather than re-waiting. It sets no checks on its own work.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 3 autonomy limits (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 3 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. The front matter limits the agent to the `cpln` tool. It never silently downgrades a setting to work around a constraint and never polls long-running operations from the AI layer.

statements.quote: **Never poll status from the AI layer.**

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 2 clarification rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all in running text. Before any state-changing command the agent establishes the target org, profile and GVC; if any is missing it stops and asks instead of falling back to the active profile.

statements.quote: If any is missing, **stop and ask. Never silently fall back to the active CLI profile.**

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 1 tied to a situation, all in running text. Before any destructive operation the agent presents a structured summary and waits for explicit confirmation, even when permissions auto-approve; anything but an unambiguous yes means stop, a delete-and-recreate technique needs its own confirmation, and destructive steps are never bundled with harmless ones.

statements.quote: Before any destructive operation, present a structured summary AND wait for explicit confirmation — **even when permissions auto-approve.**
(3) confirm — the user authorized the *goal*, not the *technique*.
Anything but an unambiguous yes means stop.
don't bundle destructive with non-destructive to slip it through.

validation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to check its own work, such as running tests, or says when the work counts as done.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 2 escalation rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all in running text. When a platform constraint blocks the user's intent, the agent surfaces it with alternatives, and on a failed or timed-out deployment it diagnoses the error instead of waiting again.
